description:
Build a reusable tmux popup flow that can launch a command in a temporary shell, send it to the background or detach it, and then restore the original session view unchanged. Use this to support starting a new tmux session unattached, optionally naming it before detaching, and other future floating command flows. Acceptance: a popup shell can capture a command, run or spawn it, and return focus to the previous session without disturbing the current layout.

Plan:
- Extract the popup execution and restore logic into a generic helper.
- Support detached session creation as one command target, with an optional naming step before detaching.
- Preserve the current session/window state so the popup behaves like a temporary overlay, not a layout change.
- Keep the existing rename popup behavior working on top of the generalized helper.
title: Generalize tmux popup workflow for detached commands
